title: Cohomology and log dualizing comparison for a given elementary nodal contraction
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $Y\to S$ and $Z\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] families with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Equip them with pairwise disjoint labelled sections $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ in the relative smooth loci, allowing $r=0$. Let $c:Y\to Z$ be a proper $S$-morphism with $ca_i=b_i$. Assume that on every geometric fibre $c$ is either an isomorphism or is an isomorphism away from one smooth irreducible component $E\simeq\mathbf P^1$ and contracts exactly $E$ to one point. Here $E$ has either two attaching nodes and no marking, or one attaching node and exactly one marking. Put $L_Y=\omega_{Y/S}(\sum a_i)$ and $L_Z=\omega_{Z/S}(\sum b_i)$, using [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum] and [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Then the structure unit $\mathcal O_Z\to c_*\mathcal O_Y$ is an isomorphism and $R^ic_*\mathcal O_Y=0$ for $i>0$. There is a canonical isomorphism $c^*L_Z\simeq L_Y$ extending the adjunction comparison off the contracted components [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $m\geq0$, it induces canonical isomorphisms $L_Z^{\otimes m}\simeq c_*L_Y^{\otimes m}$ and $R^ic_*L_Y^{\otimes m}=0$ for $i>0$, and canonical isomorphisms $R^i(Z\to S)_*L_Z^{\otimes m}\simeq R^i(Y\to S)_*L_Y^{\otimes m}$ for all $i\geq0$. For $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ these include the corresponding $k$-linear cohomology isomorphisms. The $m=0$ comparison is the structure unit, the comparisons for all $m$ preserve section multiplication, and all these assertions and comparison maps remain valid and compatible after arbitrary base change of $S$ and under isomorphisms of contraction diagrams. No stability or genus restriction is imposed; the contraction $c$ is supplied, not constructed.

proof.text: The current dualizing theorem tests nodality explicitly: on each geometric fibre the nonsmooth closed points have completed local algebra $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, and all other points are smooth. The supplied nodal families satisfy this test: their geometric fibres are reduced of pure dimension one, the nonsmooth points are closed, with residue field $\Omega$, and their completed local rings are isomorphic as rings to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; lem-trf-rational-nodal-completion-algebra, applied to an affine neighbourhood of such a point, makes this an isomorphism of complete local $\Omega$-algebras. They are also proper, flat and finitely presented, as required. Write $p:Y\to S$, $q:Z\to S$, $D_Y=\sum a_i$, $D_Z=\sum b_i$. A section in the relative smooth locus is Cartier by lem-trf-smooth-curve-section-cartier, applied to that smooth open; its image is closed in the whole proper family by lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion. Disjointness makes each sum Cartier. The divisors are relative, since each is a disjoint union of copies of $S$, so their ideal sequences remain exact under base change. The dualizing theorem supplies the canonical invertible modules and arbitrary-base-change adjunction normalization. On a contracted $E$ its degree formula gives $\deg L_Y|_E=-2+2=0$, using genus zero of $\mathbf P^1$ from sk-thm-picard-pn. Thus the degree hypotheses of the rational-contraction line-cohomology theorem hold for $\mathcal O_Y$, $L_Y$ and $L_Y^m$ for every $m\geq0$. The ideal $I_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-D_Y)$ has degree $0$ on a bridge and $-1$ on a marked tail, so that theorem applies to it as well.

source.place: Tag 0E6R; smooth Cartier sections Tag 067R; Knudsen Section 1 preceding Lemma 1.6, exceptional component degrees.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-rational-contraction-line-cohomology with $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_Y$. It gives a finitely presented quasi-coherent algebra $B=c_*\mathcal O_Y$, flat over $S$, with $R^1c_*\mathcal O_Y=0$ and arbitrary $S$-base-change compatibility. The fibres of $c$ have dimension at most one: they are points away from the exceptional image and have support $E$ at it. The general proper fibre-dimension bound therefore gives $R^ic_*\mathcal O_Y=0$ for $i>1$. All these applications also apply after every base change.

First work over a geometric point of $S$ and on an affine open $U\subset Z$. For $V=c^{-1}U$, form the affine Stein factor $V\to W=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to U$. The second map is finite: the algebra is a finite module by the preceding line-cohomology theorem. The scheme $W$ is reduced since $V$ is reduced, finite type over the algebraically closed field, and birational over $U$. Every nonexceptional component meets the isomorphism locus. The image of $E$, when present, lies in the closure of those images because $E$ has an attaching node. Surjectivity of the Stein map therefore shows that $W$ is pure of dimension one, with no extra isolated component. At a closed point of $U$ the fibre of $c$ is connected, and its surjective image in the finite fibre of $W\to U$ is connected. The other points are generic points of components, where $W\to U$ is an isomorphism. Thus all geometric fibres of this finite map are connected. By lem-trf-rational-nodal-completion-algebra $U$ passes its $k$-algebra nodal test, so the finite birational nodal criterion gives $W\simeq U$. This proves that the structure unit on each geometric $S$-fibre is an isomorphism. Return to a stalk $z\in Z$ over $s\in S$. The cokernel of $\mathcal O_Z\to B$ is finite and vanishes modulo $\mathfrak m_s$, by base change from Step 2 and faithful scalar extension to an algebraic closure. Here $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{Z,z}\subseteq\mathfrak m_z$, so vanishing modulo $\mathfrak m_s$ implies vanishing modulo the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_z$; the cited local Nakayama theorem makes the unit surjective. Its kernel is finite because $B$ is finitely presented. Since $B$ is $S$-flat, tensoring this surjection with $\kappa(s)$ preserves its kernel, which is therefore zero modulo $\mathfrak m_s$ too. Its quotient modulo $\mathfrak m_z$ is therefore zero, and the same local Nakayama theorem proves injectivity. Together with Step 2, the actual unit is $\mathcal O_Z\simeq Rc_*\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Tag 03H2, Stein factorization; nodal connected finite modification criterion from Temkin Appendix B; Knudsen Corollary 1.5 and the fibrewise Nakayama argument printed p.168.

proof.text: Apply the rational-contraction theorem to $I_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-D_Y)$, with the degrees verified in Step 1. It gives $R^1c_*I_Y=0$; the dimension bound gives all higher vanishing. The Cartier exact sequence $0\to I_Y\to\mathcal O_Y\to\bigoplus_i a_{i,*}\mathcal O_S\to0$ pushes to $0\to c_*I_Y\to\mathcal O_Z\to\bigoplus_i b_{i,*}\mathcal O_S\to0$: each $c a_i=b_i$, and a closed immersion has no higher quasi-coherent direct images. The last map is restriction, since the middle map is the structure unit, so its kernel is exactly $I_Z=\mathcal O_Z(-D_Z)$. Hence $Rc_*I_Y\simeq I_Z$ canonically. This is the derived identification induced by the restriction triangle; it holds for the empty divisor as well.

source.place: Cartier ideal sequence; Knudsen Section 1, printed pp.167--168, comparison of the negative marking ideals.

proof.text: Apply relative trace-duality to $F=I_Y$. Both $F$ and $Rc_*F=I_Z$ are invertible, hence perfect. Cancelling the common shift $[1]$ in its isomorphism gives $Rc_*L_Y\simeq L_Z$, since $R\mathcal Hom(I_Y,\omega_{Y/S})=I_Y^\vee\otimes\omega_{Y/S}=L_Y$, and likewise on $Z$. Denote its degree-zero inverse by $\beta:L_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}c_*L_Y$. The rational-contraction theorem gives a surjective adjunction evaluation $c^*c_*L_Y\to L_Y$, because the exceptional degrees are zero. Composing with $c^*\beta$ gives a surjection $\alpha:c^*L_Z\to L_Y$. A surjection between invertible modules is an isomorphism: after trivializing them it is multiplication by an element generating the local ring, hence by a unit. The trace normalization says that $\alpha$ agrees with the adjunction comparison wherever $c$ is an isomorphism. This constructs the canonical log-dualizing isomorphism, rather than merely comparing component degrees.

source.place: Tags 0A9Q and 0GEV, applied to the perfect marking ideal; relative trace base change Tags 0E5X and 0E6C in spaces-duality.tex; Knudsen comparison preceding Lemma 1.6.

proof.text: For $m\geq0$ take $\alpha^{\otimes m}:c^*(L_Z^{\otimes m})\simeq L_Y^{\otimes m}$. Its adjoint $\beta_m:L_Z^{\otimes m}\to c_*L_Y^{\otimes m}$ is an isomorphism. For a line power, $Lc^*(L_Z^{\otimes m})=c^*(L_Z^{\otimes m})$: locally its rank-one free representative already computes derived pullback, without any flatness assumption on $c$. The perfect projection formula with $E=\mathcal O_Y$ and $P=L_Z^{\otimes m}$ identifies its derived version with the tensor product of the actual structure unit $\mathcal O_Z\to Rc_*\mathcal O_Y$ and $P$, followed by $Rc_*(\alpha^{\otimes m})$. Both maps are isomorphisms by Steps 3 and 5. Thus $Rc_*L_Y^{\otimes m}\simeq L_Z^{\otimes m}$, giving the stated direct-image isomorphism and all higher vanishing. For $m=0$ the map is exactly the structure unit. The use of the adjoint of $\alpha^{\otimes m}$ fixes the comparison maps without choices.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; Knudsen Lemma 1.6(a),(b), with the additional m=0 unit case.

proof.text: Apply $Rq_*$ to the derived isomorphism of Step 6 and use the canonical direct-image compositor $R(qc)_*\simeq Rq_*Rc_*$. Its degree-$i$ cohomology gives $R^iq_*L_Z^{\otimes m}\simeq R^ip_*L_Y^{\otimes m}$ for every $i\geq0$. Over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ this is precisely the $k$-linear cohomology comparison. For local sections $s$ and $t$ of tensor powers, both multiplication routes take $s\otimes t$ to $\alpha^{\otimes(m+n)}c^*(s\otimes t)$, since $\alpha^{\otimes(m+n)}=\alpha^{\otimes m}\otimes\alpha^{\otimes n}$. Adjunction therefore makes the direct-image comparisons preserve section multiplication, including its unit.

For any $S_{new}\to S$, the geometric fibre hypotheses, including the explicit nodal local-algebra test in Step 1, remain exactly the same, so Steps 1--7 apply to the pulled-back diagram. The dualizing and divisor comparisons in Step 1 commute with this base change. The line-cohomology theorem makes the units and the marking-ideal identification of Steps 2--4 commute with arbitrary base change. Relative trace-duality makes $\beta$ in Step 5 commute as well; the adjunction evaluation defining $\alpha$ commutes with the same canonical maps. Tensoring and taking adjuncts then give the identical $\beta_m$ after base change, and the derived compositor gives commutative squares on relative cohomology. These are compatibilities with the canonical base-change maps; no assertion that each separate $R^iq_*L_Z^m$ has invertible ordinary base-change map is needed. All constructions (unit, restriction to labelled sections, trace, evaluation, tensor powers, compositor) are natural under isomorphisms of contraction diagrams. Their identity and composition laws give the required iterated compatibilities.
